column1: # The files deposited to the SRA, and what they must hash to.
# BioProject PRJNA1513130. One run per replicate; the BioSample accession for
# each sample_id lives in the samplesheets, which are where per-sample keys
# belong -- do not duplicate it here, or the two will drift.
# These are the FASTQs the analysis in the manuscript was run on, so the md5
# below is the strongest available statement that a downloaded file is the file
# we analysed. bin/fetch_ena_reads.sh checks it, and the check only holds for
# ENA's `submitted_ftp` copy: SRA regenerates `fastq_ftp` from its own archive,
# which is the same sequence but not the same bytes. The script says which one
# it used.
# reads and bases are the totals BEFORE and AFTER masking alike -- masking
# replaces bases with N in place and removes nothing, so these are also the
# numbers reported in the manuscript. See results/summary/human_masking.tsv.
# Columns
#   sample_id  key into the samplesheets
#   filename   name as submitted; ENA reports it in `submitted_ftp`
#   bytes      size of the submitted .gz
#   md5        md5 of the submitted .gz, verified by the depositor before upload
#   reads      records in the file
#   bases      total sequence length
